input: Under this inventory policy for a spare motor, the safety stock is 741 units and the reorder point is 5671 units. Mean demand is 2465 units per week and the standard deviation of demand is 635 units per week; the replenishment lead time is 2 weeks. The safety stock represents the cover that is held against demand varying around its mean during those 2 weeks, and it is sized to a 95% cycle service level, which can be understood as the probability that a replenishment cycle ends without a stockout. An order that is placed when stock falls to 5671 units covers the demand that is expected over the lead time, at 2465 units per week, with the 741 units of safety stock held behind it. It is important to note that the calculation treats demand as normal and independent between weeks, and seasonal peaks are excluded. The stated service level therefore describes ordinary weeks only; in a peak week, demand above the mean will consume the safety stock sooner than the policy assumes, and cover that the 95% figure appears to promise is not there. Overall, the policy is a statement about averages, and its figures stand or fall with the demand record behind them.
